title: Tenant-proportional graceful yielding with KV locality hints
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Goal: Implement a tenant-proportional graceful yielding policy for the continuous batcher that reclaims GPU memory/KV residency with minimal SLO impact. The policy should use per-tenant proportional shares (weighted by recent SLA usage and priority) and KV locality hints to avoid evicting hot prefixes. This ticket covers the scheduler algorithm, KV hint propagation, memory pressure thresholds, and an experimental rollout path with canary telemetry.
background: Current preemption is binary: high-priority requests interrupt lower-priority ones and we evict KV entries bluntly, which causes tail-latency spikes and model refill churn. Previous work (ENG-7421, ENG-17283) implemented SLO-aware preemption primitives and KV accounting; this ticket synthesizes those primitives into a proportional yielding policy that targets fairness and minimized KV churn.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler implements tenant-proportional soft-yield: when GPU memory pressure exceeds threshold, reduce per-tenant token budgets proportionally to weight rather than hard-killing batches.
KV hints API implemented: frontend/request router can attach KV-locality hints (prefix hotness score) that the scheduler uses to prefer evicting cold entries.

End-to-end tests: stress scenarios reproduce <5% SLO breach rate increase for P1 customers at 95th percentile latency compared to baseline, and fairness metric (Jain's index across tenants) improves versus current preempt-all baseline.
Benchmarks: memory reclamation path reclaims required memory within configured time window without >2x increase in token compute cost from KV misses.
Canary rollout config and rollback playbook documented in runbook (links included).

design_notes: We decided against a pure market-based scheduler due to high oscillation risk on short-lived requests. Instead we model proportional yield as a leaky-bucket scaling factor per tenant computed from a 1-min EWMA of recent consumed tokens and SLA weight. Yield signal is sent as 'soft throttle' to batch assembly stage, which will prefer deferring a tenant's request by up to 40ms before hard preemption. KV locality hints are lightweight integers (0-3) representing hot/cold buckets computed at request entry; eviction cost = estimated refill tokens * locality_penalty. Trade-offs: this minimizes KV churn and keeps tail latency stable but can increase average queuing time for lower-weight tenants under sustained pressure.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: API + accounting (2 weeks) — add locality_hint propagation and per-tenant EWMA counters. Phase 2: Scheduler core (3 weeks) — implement proportional factor, soft-yield signal, and memory reclamation integration. Phase 3: Telemetry + tests (2 weeks) — integrate dashboards, run load tests, validate SLAs. Phase 4: Canary rollout (1 week) — roll to 3% of serving capacity, monitor for regressions and iterate.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly aggressive soft-yield could cause request pile-up and head-of-line blocking. Mitigation: limit soft-yield interval and provide backpressure to ingress with early reject thresholds.
Risk: Incorrect locality hints reduce effectiveness. Mitigation: conservative default hint (neutral) and perf analysis in canary to tune thresholds.
Risk: Complexity increases scheduler CPU overhead. Mitigation: microbench scheduler path and ensure computations are O(1) per tenant using fixed-size sliding-window aggregators.
Risk: Eviction cost estimates understate refill cost. Mitigation: include safety multiplier (1.5x) and track actual refill tokens to adjust model online.
Risk: Unexpected customer impact during rollout. Mitigation: start with non-critical tenants, enable auto-rollback on spikes, and expose opt-out flag for enterprise customers.
Risk: Fairness metric gaming by tenants. Mitigation: cap per-tenant weight changes to prevent sudden jumps and tie weight updates to verified billing/SLA changes only.
Risk: Interactions with Dedicated GPU isolation. Mitigation: Dedicated pools default to conservative policy (no cross-tenant proportional yield) unless tenant opts in.
Risk: Security review required for any telemetry containing tenant IDs. Mitigation: redact tenant identifiers in public dashboards; only hashed IDs used in metrics pipelines.
telemetry_and_dashboards: New dashboard: 'Proportional Yield Health' showing per-tenant throttle, 95/99 latency, KV eviction rate, reuse-rate, and fairness index (link: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/proportional-yield)
Alert: >3% delta in baseline SLO breaches in 5m window triggers rollback (alert in PagerDuty)
Metric: 'scheduler.yield_factor' per tenant sampled at 1s granularity
Metric: 'kv.evictions_by_hint' broken down by locality_hint bucket
test_plan: Unit tests for EWMA counters and yield computation. Integration tests that simulate mixed tenant loads with KV-hot prefixes. Performance bench runs on 8-GPU p4d-like cluster and smaller 1-GPU dev profile. Regression test asserting <5% SLO breach delta and improved Jain's fairness index compared to current preempt-all baseline.
